::: {#sol-init-scale}

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
def last_layer_sd(scale, depth=10, width=256):
    # scale(n_in) gives the standard deviation of the weights of a layer with n_in inputs.
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    h = x_train
    for layer in range(depth):
        n_in = h.shape[1]
        weight = scale(n_in) * torch.randn(width, n_in)
        h = torch.relu(h @ weight.T)
    return h.std().item()


init_sd = {
    "small": last_layer_sd(lambda n_in: 0.01),
    "he": last_layer_sd(lambda n_in: math.sqrt(2 / n_in)),
    "large": last_layer_sd(lambda n_in: 0.2),
    "pixels": x_train.std().item(),
}
print(init_sd)
```

The pixels have standard deviation `r sprintf("%.2f", py$init_sd[["pixels"]])`.
After 10 layers,
$\sigma = 0.01$ leaves values with standard deviation about $10^{`r round(log10(py$init_sd[["small"]]))`}$,
$\sigma = 0.2$ gives about $10^{`r round(log10(py$init_sd[["large"]]))`}$,
and $\sigma = \sqrt{2 / n_{\text{in}}}$ gives `r sprintf("%.2f", py$init_sd[["he"]])`,
close to where it started.
Each layer multiplies the typical size of the values by about $\sigma \sqrt{n_{\text{in}} / 2}$:
the weighted sum of $n_{\text{in}}$ values has variance proportional to $n_{\text{in}} \sigma^2$,
and the [ReLU](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-relu) zeroes about half of the results.
That factor is 1 for $\sigma^2 = 2 / n_{\text{in}}$,
which is [He initialization](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/backpropagation.html#def-he-initialization) [@he2015delving].
Since [backpropagation](backpropagation.qmd#def-backpropagation) multiplies by the same weight matrices on the way back,
the [gradients](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/linear-regression.html#def-gradient) shrink or grow layer by layer in the same way.

:::
